governed_construct: An authentication operation in the file: a call or construction that signs a user in or up, verifies a credential or token, or registers an authentication strategy/provider (e.g. signIn, signUp, authenticateUser, InitiateAuthCommand, token verify, passport.use, NextAuth(...), auth0 auth(...), bcrypt.compare + jwt.sign login). Each such operation is one instance, judged by the module its callee is actually bound to.
interpretation: The rule requires that authentication be performed through Amazon Cognito. An instance conforms when the identifier/object performing the auth operation resolves to a Cognito module: aws-amplify/auth (Amplify Auth backed by a Cognito user pool), amazon-cognito-identity-js, @aws-sdk/client-cognito-identity-provider, or aws-jwt-verify's CognitoJwtVerifier for verifying Cognito tokens. An instance violates when it resolves to any other mechanism: Firebase Auth, Passport, NextAuth/Auth.js, Auth0, or a hand-rolled password check plus JWT issuance, or a local function that posts credentials to a custom endpoint. Files with no authentication operation (e.g. plain S3 or utility code) are NOT_APPLICABLE even if they use other AWS SDK clients. Edge decisions: binding decides, not names - a local function named like an Amplify call that shadows the import is not Cognito, and Cognito functions imported under Firebase-like aliases are still Cognito; verifying Cognito-issued JWTs with aws-jwt-verify counts as conforming authentication.
